story: Milwaukee City Hall was finished in 1895 and was the city's tallest building until 1973. Henry C. Koch designed it in the Flemish Renaissance Revival style, based on city halls in Germany and on local buildings. It became a National Historic Landmark in 2005.

It stands on 2,584 white pine piles driven into marshy ground. The main block rises eight stories, and the tower reaches 350 feet, with clock faces flanked by four beer stein turrets. A fire in October 1929 damaged the upper tower, which was rebuilt.

The tower holds a 22,500-pound bell named for Solomon Juneau, Milwaukee's first mayor, which was hoisted up in 1896. The tower's lighted marquee appeared in the opening of the TV show Laverne & Shirley, and it was removed in 1988.
stops.disputed: Many people think a tall old building must sit on solid rock. Wikipedia says this one stands on thousands of wooden piles in marshy ground.

claims.t: Milwaukee City Hall was finished in 1895.
The tower has never been damaged by fire.
claims.why: Wikipedia says a fire in October 1929 damaged the upper tower, which was rebuilt.

story: The Mitchell Building is a five-story bank and insurance building in the Second Empire style. It was built in 1876 and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

Alexander Mitchell was a Scottish immigrant who came to the United States in 1839. He led an insurance company, a railroad and a bank, and he served two terms in the U.S. House. He hired architect E. Townsend Mix to design the building. Its first-floor walls are gray Minnesota granite and the upper walls are limestone, with a mansard roof and an ornate central tower.

It is believed to stand on the site of the home of Solomon Juneau, who founded Milwaukee in the 1830s. Mitchell's bank stayed there until 1930. The exterior remains highly intact, though much of the fancy interior has disappeared with remodeling.
stops.fact: Its first-floor walls are Minnesota granite.
stops.disputed: Many people think fancy old banks were rebuilt long ago. Wikipedia says the exterior of this one remains highly intact.

claims.t: The Mitchell Building was built in 1876.
The Mitchell Building was always a hotel.
claims.why: It was built as a bank and insurance building.

story: Milwaukee Soldiers Home, known as Old Main, is one of three soldiers homes that have survived in the United States. It was built to help Civil War soldiers recover. It was completed in 1867 and went by several names, including National Asylum for Disabled Soldiers.

There are 24 other buildings on the grounds, and together they form the Northwestern Branch, National Home for Disabled Volunteer Soldiers Historic District. Old Main was unoccupied from 1989, fell into disrepair and was scheduled for demolition.

A 2011 campaign succeeded in getting it designated a National Historic Landmark. In 2019 a company was hired to update the building, and the Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority helped finance the restoration.
stops.fact: It was scheduled for demolition, then saved.

claims.t: Old Main has been in use ever since it was built.

story: The Milwaukee Auditorium was built in 1909 where the Milwaukee Industrial Exposition Building had stood before a fire destroyed it in 1905. The cornerstone was laid on August 1, 1908, and the building was dedicated on September 21, 1909.

It held 13,520 people and had almost 105,000 square feet of exhibition space. Elizabeth Plankinton donated a pipe organ. It hosted concerts, circuses, political rallies and sports events, from John Philip Sousa and Enrico Caruso to modern stars, and sitting presidents from Taft to Clinton gave speeches there.
A renovation from 2001 to 2003 changed its name to the Milwaukee Theatre. A naming rights deal changed it to the Miller High Life Theatre in 2017. Today it seats 4,086 people.
stops.fact: Presidents from Taft to Clinton spoke here.
stops.disputed: Many people think the Milwaukee Theatre has always had that name. Wikipedia says it was originally the Milwaukee Auditorium.

claims.t: The Milwaukee Auditorium was dedicated in 1909.
The building has always been called the Milwaukee Theatre.
claims.why: It was originally the Milwaukee Auditorium.
